subject: Agriculture
title: Resistant Varieties
description: A micro-lesson that makes Resistant Varieties usable.

hook.text: Breeding disease resistance into crops is the cheapest, most sustainable disease control. No sprays needed.

buildup.text: Plants have immune systems—they recognize pathogen molecules and activate defense genes.

discovery.text: Breeders screen thousands of plant lines against diseases, selecting those with natural resistance genes.

twist.text: Single-gene resistance typically breaks within 3–5 years as pathogens evolve to overcome it.

climax.text: Stacking multiple resistance genes into one variety makes it harder for pathogens to evolve past all defenses.

punchline.text: One lock is easy to pick. Five locks together buy decades.

quiz.question: Why does single-gene disease resistance often fail within a few years?
options: Pathogens evolve to overcome the single defense
